features.name: content_length_log
features.description: Logarithmic transformation of the number of words in the content to compress the long-tailed distribution.
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses extreme values in article length, providing a smoother, more normally distributed feature that improves linear SVM margin stability.

features.name: lexical_diversity_score
features.description: Composite index of vocabulary richness, calculated as the product of unique token rate and non-stop unique token rate.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a non-linear interaction between two diversity metrics, allowing the linear model to separate highly repetitive text from in-depth vocabulary usage.

features.name: visual_media_ratio
features.description: Ratio of visual media (images and videos) to the total number of media and links.
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalizes visual content counts into a bounded [0,1] ratio, which scales perfectly for linear models and captures the visual-heaviness of an article.

features.name: self_reference_ratio
features.description: Proportion of hyperlinks that point to the publisher's own domain, clipped to a maximum of 1.0.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a bounded continuous measure of self-promotion, helping the SVM establish margins based on internal vs. external linking behavior.

features.name: sentiment_polarity_intensity
features.description: Absolute magnitude of the global sentiment polarity, representing the intensity of opinion regardless of positive or negative direction.
features.expected_model_benefit: Converts a signed sentiment score into a continuous severity measure of opinionation, useful for separating neutral reporting from highly opinionated pieces.

features.name: positive_to_negative_word_ratio
features.description: Ratio of the rate of positive words to the rate of negative words, with a small constant added to the denominator to prevent division by zero.
features.expected_model_benefit: Expresses the relative balance of positive to negative tone as a continuous ratio, aiding linear separation based on overall emotional skew.

features.name: subjectivity_sentiment_interaction
features.description: Interaction between global subjectivity and global sentiment polarity.
features.expected_model_benefit: Weights sentiment by subjectivity, creating an interaction term that allows a linear model to capture content that is both highly subjective and strongly polarized.

features.name: keyword_density
features.description: Number of keywords normalized by the logarithmic length of the article content.
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalizes keyword counts against article length, providing a density metric that scales well and prevents long articles from dominating the feature space.

features.name: title_clickbait_score
features.description: Semantic evaluation of the article title to determine the presence of clickbait patterns, such as listicles, sensationalism, or phrases like 'Must Reads' and 'Missed'.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a continuous semantic score evaluating engagement tactics, adding non-linear semantic value that a linear model can use as a direct projection.

features.name: title_digital_domain_score
features.description: Semantic evaluation of how strongly the article title relates to digital media, apps, software, gadgets, or internet culture.
features.expected_model_benefit: Evaluates the semantic relevance of the title to digital topics, providing a direct linear projection for topic-based margins without relying on raw text.

features.name: title_pop_culture_score
features.description: Semantic evaluation of how strongly the article title relates to viral media, memes, celebrities, or general pop culture.
features.expected_model_benefit: Offers a continuous semantic feature for topic separation, allowing the SVM to linearly weight the presence of pop-culture themes.

features.name: content_complexity_index
features.description: Product of average token length and the rate of non-stop words, serving as a proxy for reading complexity.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines word length and non-stop word frequency into a single complexity index, helping the linear model distinguish between simple and complex writing styles.
